title: Mock 4 · Process and Paperwork
blurb: Deal process, due diligence, PPM and documents, with one caselet.

questions.q: Venture capital investing primarily involves:
options: Direct investment in early-stage businesses with high growth potential and high mortality risk
Lending to large corporates against fixed assets
questions.explanation: Venture capital is about direct investment in infant companies yet to grow fully; they are highly risky due to high mortality rates.
hints: Wrong: that is a traditional investment.
Correct: VC targets start-ups/early-stage ventures.
Wrong: that is bank-style lending.
Wrong: traditional, low-risk investment.

questions.q: Who made the USD 292 million investment in Bharti Televentures that the workbook calls arguably the first characteristic private equity transaction in India?
questions.explanation: The first characteristic PE transaction in India is arguably the USD 292 million investment by Warburg Pincus in Bharti Televentures, exited via IPO in 2002.
hints: Wrong: KKR's landmark deal was the Flextronics buyout (2006).
Wrong: Blackstone led later buyouts.
Wrong: Actis is mentioned among buyout funds.
Correct: Warburg Pincus, with a successful IPO exit in 2002.

questions.q: A Special Situation Fund may act as a resolution applicant under which law?
questions.explanation: Special Situation Fund means a Category I AIF that invests in special situation assets and may act as a resolution applicant under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.
hints: Wrong: repealed and irrelevant.
Wrong: IBC is the cited law.
Wrong: unrelated.
Correct: SSFs may act as resolution applicants under IBC 2016.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a disqualification under the 'fit and proper person' criteria for a sponsor?
options: A pending charge sheet in a criminal complaint
Having earned profits from a previous fund
Being found of unsound mind by a competent court
questions.explanation: The fit and proper criteria disqualify a person with pending criminal charge sheet, restraint/debarment orders, insolvency/wilful defaulter status, or unsound mind finding.
hints: Wrong: a pending criminal charge sheet disqualifies.
Correct: profits are not a disqualification.
Wrong: wilful defaulter status disqualifies.
Wrong: unsound mind finding disqualifies.

questions.q: An individual's accreditation as an Accredited Investor through the income route requires annual income of at least:
questions.explanation: Individual/HUF/family trust/proprietorship/partnership: annual income at least ₹2 crore; or net worth ₹7.5 crore (₹3.75 crore financial); or ₹1 crore income + ₹5 crore net worth (₹2.5 crore financial).
hints: Correct: ₹2 crore annual income alone suffices.
Wrong: ₹1 crore works only with net worth ₹5 crore (₹2.5 crore financial).
Wrong: too low.
Wrong: ₹5 crore is a net-worth figure in the combined route.

questions.q: Which entity issues the Accreditation Certificate to an Accredited Investor?
options: An accreditation agency such as a subsidiary of a recognised stock exchange or depository
questions.explanation: Accreditation Agency means a subsidiary of a recognised stock exchange or of a depository or any other entity specified by SEBI.
hints: Wrong: SEBI does not issue individual certificates.
Wrong: managers may provisionally onboard but cannot certify.
Correct: accreditation agencies are subsidiaries of exchanges/depositories or SEBI-specified entities.
Wrong: banks are not accreditation agencies.

questions.q: Which certification must at least one key personnel in the key investment team of a Category I/II AIF manager hold?
questions.explanation: At least one key personnel must have NISM-Series-XIX-C or XIX-D, and the same person must also have a specified professional qualification.
hints: Wrong: XIX-A is for distributors.
Wrong: V-A is for mutual fund distributors.
Correct: XIX-C (AIF Managers) or XIX-D (Cat I & II AIF Managers).
Wrong: III-C is for the compliance officer.

questions.q: Under a pure offshore fund structure, the fund's investments into India are typically made through:
options: Registration as a Category I AIF
Registration under the SEBI FVCI Regulations or directly under the FDI route
questions.explanation: Since the fund is incorporated outside India it requires registration under SEBI (FVCI) Regulations; alternatively it can invest directly under the FDI policy.
hints: Wrong: the fund is incorporated outside India.
Wrong: unrelated.
Correct: FVCI registration or the FDI route.
Wrong: unrelated.

questions.q: Under the LLP structure for an AIF, how many designated partners must the LLP have at a minimum?
questions.explanation: Every LLP must have at least two 'designated partners' responsible for its conduct and compliances.
hints: Wrong: too few.
Correct: every LLP must have at least two designated partners.
Wrong: not the requirement.
Wrong: not the requirement.

questions.q: Which method improves on IRR by using a realistic opportunity cost for discounting capital calls and compounding distributions?
questions.explanation: MIRR considers the opportunity cost of funds at an appropriate rate; in the illustration IRR is 22% while MIRR at 10% is 18.7%.
hints: Correct: Modified IRR uses an appropriate opportunity cost.
Wrong: DPI is a cash multiple.
Wrong: PIC is a drawdown ratio.
Wrong: ROI ignores time value.

questions.q: Rank the following claims from highest to lowest priority in a borrower's insolvency: equity, unsecured debt, secured senior debt, preference capital.
options: Secured senior debt > unsecured debt > preference capital > equity
Unsecured debt > secured senior debt > equity > preference
questions.explanation: Secured senior debt has the first claim, unsecured debt ranks lowest among debt; all debt has priority over preference capital, which ranks higher than equity.
hints: Correct: all debt ranks above preference, which ranks above equity.
Wrong: reverse order.
Wrong: secured ranks above unsecured; preference above equity.
Wrong: debt ranks above preference.

questions.q: Who usually carries out the financial due diligence review (DDR) of an investee company on behalf of the AIF manager?
options: An accounting firm or investment bank engaged by the manager
questions.explanation: Financial DDR is usually carried out on behalf of the manager by an accounting firm or investment bank; legal DDR by a law firm.
hints: Wrong: the trustee does not conduct DDR.
Correct: financial DDR is usually done by an accounting firm or investment bank.
Wrong: independence would be compromised.
Wrong: SEBI does not do deal DDR.

questions.q: The Compliance Test Report (CTR) must be submitted by the manager to the sponsor/trustee within how many days from the end of the financial year?
questions.explanation: The CTR shall be submitted by the manager to the sponsor (and trustee) within 30 days from the end of the financial year; comments within 30 days; reply within 15 days.
hints: Wrong: 15 days is the manager's time to reply to comments.
Correct: within 30 days of FY end.
Wrong: not prescribed.
Wrong: 180 days is for the annual report to investors.

questions.q: Which data must AIFs submit to benchmarking agencies?
options: Scheme-wise valuation and cash flow data for schemes that completed at least one year from first close
Only audited balance sheets of the manager
Daily NAV of all schemes from launch
questions.explanation: AIFs, for all schemes that completed at least one year from first close, shall report scheme-wise valuation and cash flow data to the benchmarking agencies.
hints: Correct: scheme-wise valuation and cash-flow data after one year from first close.
Wrong: not the required data.
Wrong: confidential and irrelevant.
Wrong: AIFs have no daily NAV.

questions.q: A pension fund wants medium risk, steady long-term income and interim payouts. Which AIF profile best fits?
options: A debt fund investing in secured debentures of operational, lease-yielding real estate SPVs
A land-bank acquisition real estate equity fund
A fund taking leveraged long-short positions in derivatives
questions.explanation: Case 8.1 shows a pension fund seeking medium risk and interim payouts is best matched with an alternative debt fund in operational lease-backed SPVs.
hints: Correct: steady cash flow and moderate risk match the pension fund.
Wrong: high risk, no interim income.
Wrong: illiquid, lumpy returns.
Wrong: that is a Category III style strategy.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the key criteria for evaluating a fund manager listed in the workbook?
options: Performance track record in delivering returns
Instances of conflict of interest or regulatory non-compliance
The manager's personal social media following
questions.explanation: Key criteria: prior fund experience, return track record, strategy expertise, exit expertise, litigations/write-offs, conflicts and non-compliance.
hints: Wrong: track record is a key criterion.
Wrong: exit expertise is a key criterion.
Wrong: conduct issues are a key criterion.
Correct: not a criterion in the workbook.

questions.q: Through whom must a regular AIF scheme file its PPM with SEBI?
questions.explanation: The PPM shall be filed with SEBI along with fees through a merchant banker, who exercises independent due diligence and gives a certificate.
hints: Correct: the PPM is filed through a merchant banker with a due diligence certificate.
Wrong: exchanges do not file PPMs.
Wrong: not the filing route.
Wrong: custodians safekeep securities.

questions.q: The contribution (subscription) agreement of an AIF trust is entered into between:
options: The trustee and the investment manager only
Each investor, the trustee and the investment manager
questions.explanation: The Contribution Agreement is entered into between each contributor (investor), the trustee and the investment manager.
hints: Wrong: that is the IMA.
Wrong: SEBI is not a party.
Correct: investor, trustee and manager.
Wrong: the distributor is not a party.

questions.q: Within what period must the findings of the annual PPM audit be communicated to the trustee/board, the manager's board and SEBI?
options: 6 months from the end of the financial year
1 month from the end of the financial year
30 days from the end of each quarter
1 year from the end of the financial year
questions.explanation: The PPM audit findings with corrective steps shall be communicated within 6 months from the end of the financial year.
hints: Correct: within 6 months of FY end.
Wrong: 1 month is for intimating PPM changes.
Wrong: not prescribed.
Wrong: too late.

questions.q: The limited Quarterly Activity Report must be submitted by AIFs on the SEBI Intermediary Portal within:
options: 30 calendar days from the end of each quarter
15 calendar days from the end of each quarter
7 days from the end of each quarter
45 days from the end of each quarter
questions.explanation: A limited Quarterly Activity Report shall be submitted within 15 calendar days from the end of each quarter (none separately for the March quarter).
hints: Wrong: 30 days applies to the Annual Activity Report.
Correct: within 15 calendar days.
Wrong: 7 days relates to compiling complaint data.
Wrong: not prescribed.

questions.q: To claim benefits under a DTAA, a non-resident investor in an AIF must, among other things, obtain:
options: A valid Tax Residency Certificate from its country of residence, renewed annually
questions.explanation: A non-resident is not entitled to DTAA relief unless it obtains a TRC from the government of its country of residence; it must be renewed annually.
hints: Wrong: SEBI does not certify tax residency.
Wrong: unrelated.
Wrong: unrelated.
Correct: a TRC is mandatory for treaty relief.

questions.q: In the case, the document Nilgiri received first, summarising AgriSense in a few pages to test preliminary fit, is called a:
questions.explanation: The investment banker sends a 'teaser' or 'flier' (a brief 1-3 page summary) to prospective funds to check preliminary fit.
hints: Wrong: comes later and states proposed terms.
Wrong: a definitive agreement signed at the end.
Wrong: comes after the term sheet.
Correct: a teaser or flier is a brief 1-3 page summary.
questions.case: Nilgiri Ventures Fund (a Category I VC fund) received a 2-page teaser from an investment bank about AgriSense, an unlisted agri-tech start-up. After signing an NDA it received the information memorandum, met the management, and its investment team presented a short proposal to the Investment Committee. Nilgiri will be a 20% minority shareholder. Its main worries are: (i) the founders selling out early, (ii) a future round at a lower valuation, and (iii) being unable to sell a small minority stake at exit. The founders want the deal closed quickly.

questions.q: Which right best addresses Nilgiri's worry about the founders selling out early to a third party?
questions.explanation: Tag-along makes shares more difficult to sell because investors bank on founders and do not want them to exit while they remain invested; often combined with ROFR and lock-in.
hints: Wrong: drag-along helps Nilgiri force a sale, not stop founders exiting.
Wrong: applies on liquidation.
Correct: tag-along lets Nilgiri sell alongside and makes founders' shares harder to sell.
Wrong: unrelated.
questions.case: Nilgiri Ventures Fund (a Category I VC fund) received a 2-page teaser from an investment bank about AgriSense, an unlisted agri-tech start-up. After signing an NDA it received the information memorandum, met the management, and its investment team presented a short proposal to the Investment Committee. Nilgiri will be a 20% minority shareholder. Its main worries are: (i) the founders selling out early, (ii) a future round at a lower valuation, and (iii) being unable to sell a small minority stake at exit. The founders want the deal closed quickly.

questions.q: Which protection addresses Nilgiri's concern about a future financing round at a lower valuation?
questions.explanation: A ratchet compensates the investor against additional dilution in a down round by issuing new shares at no or minimal cost.
hints: Wrong: ROFO governs share transfers.
Wrong: key man is a fund-level clause.
Correct: a ratchet issues extra shares to compensate in a down round.
Wrong: clawback is between fund investors and manager.
questions.case: Nilgiri Ventures Fund (a Category I VC fund) received a 2-page teaser from an investment bank about AgriSense, an unlisted agri-tech start-up. After signing an NDA it received the information memorandum, met the management, and its investment team presented a short proposal to the Investment Committee. Nilgiri will be a 20% minority shareholder. Its main worries are: (i) the founders selling out early, (ii) a future round at a lower valuation, and (iii) being unable to sell a small minority stake at exit. The founders want the deal closed quickly.

questions.q: As a 20% minority holder, which right will help Nilgiri sell a stake large enough to attract a control premium at exit?
options: Right to a board observer seat
questions.explanation: A drag-along is usually insisted on when the AIF is a minority investor so the stake offered is large enough to attract a control or strategic premium.
hints: Wrong: protects shareholding in new issues.
Wrong: governance right, not exit.
Wrong: information right, not exit.
Correct: drag-along obliges promoters to sell to the same buyer on the same terms.
